segments.he: וְלֹא אֶת חִיצַת הַקָּנִים שֶׁהִיא בֵּית רוֹבַע. וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּקַטִּינֵי. אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא חִיצַת הַקָּנִים בִּלְבַד; אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ עֲרוּגָה קְטַנָּה שֶׁל בְּשָׂמִים, וְיֵשׁ לָהּ שֵׁם בִּפְנֵי עַצְמָהּ – אֵינָהּ נִמְכֶּרֶת עִמָּהּ. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְהוּא דְּקָרוּ לָהּ: ״וַורְדָּא דִפְלָנְיָא״.
segments.en: The mishna teaches that one who sells a field has «not» sold «the cluster of reeds that» occupy «a beit rova.» The Gemara comments: «And» this is so «even though they are thin,» as since they occupy the area of a beit rova they are considered a separate entity and are not part of the field. Concerning this ruling, «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba says» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan says:» It is «not only a cluster of reeds» that is considered a separate entity, and therefore not included in the sale; «rather, even a small garden bed of spices» that does not occupy the area of a beit rova «but has a distinct name is not sold» along «with» the field. «Rav Pappa said:» What «this» means is «that» people «call it the roses [vardda] of so-and-so,» thereby establishing for it a name of its own.
